functional.designIntent: Each purchasable access is a believable failed piece of rural infrastructure. It blocks a clear seam between districts without pretending that every map edge is a pile of rocks.

accesses.role: Farm service entrance; first expansion seam
accesses.gameplayMotivation: The broad agricultural track reads as a usable cart route and retains a horse-safe clearance once unlocked.
accesses.interferenceRisk: Fence leaves must not narrow the open route below 4.8 m.

accesses.gameplayMotivation: A collapsed log boom belongs at the yard road and establishes a visibly heavier upgrade than the farm gate.
accesses.interferenceRisk: Loose logs cannot project into the route after the blocker sinks.

accesses.gameplayMotivation: A narrower wrought-iron gate and stone piers make the cemetery boundary legible rather than an arbitrary wall opening.
accesses.interferenceRisk: The gate silhouette must not cover the church approach or grave sightlines.

accesses.gameplayMotivation: A timber emergency barricade naturally guards the only engineered creek crossing; the existing stone bridge is retained as the revealed crossing.
accesses.interferenceRisk: Keep bridge deck and its approaches free of blocking decoration.

accesses.gameplayMotivation: A deliberate timber fall makes the deep-woods boundary read as weather damage, not a manufactured gate.
accesses.interferenceRisk: The fallen-tree cluster must remain inside its closure box and leave no invisible side wall.

accesses.gameplayMotivation: A broken farm cart and movable fence are credible maintenance clutter between working districts.
accesses.interferenceRisk: Do not obscure the road split or produce a second visual landmark competing with the sawmill entrance.

accesses.gameplayMotivation: A small iron wicket communicates a secondary pedestrian route out of the churchyard instead of a second generic full-size gate.
accesses.interferenceRisk: Keep silhouette lower than the churchyard entrance and do not block the cemetery perimeter path.

aesthetic.styleAnchor: Storm-damaged rural European village: functional farm timber, mossed stone, blackened iron and restrained warm safety light.

accesses.treatment: Two sagging fence leaves and working posts; no destination billboard.
Low irregular log boom with a stacked cut-wood witness pile.
Existing iron leaf between stone piers; cold metal against church stone.
Temporary flood barricade at the permanent stone bridge, removed on purchase.
Felled trunks and branch-like stacked timber; no man-made gate.
Collapsed farm route marker built from fence and recovered wheel.
Small pedestrian iron wicket with restrained stone sidewalls.
